name: getVDigest
title: Set a vectorised function for creating hash function digests

origin.description: Return a function that hashes each element of its input with one algorithm.

arguments.name: algo
arguments.text: The hash algorithm. A unique prefix is accepted. md5 is the default.

arguments.name: errormode
arguments.text: stop aborts. warn warns and returns NA. silent returns NULL.

origin.details: The returned function takes the same arguments as digest, except raw is always false. An atomic vector is hashed one element at a time, so getVDigest()(1:5) matches digest of each integer. A raw vector is one object. To hash a list the way digest(list("a")) does, pass list(list("a")).
origin.value: A function that returns a character vector of hashes.

translation.description: Return a function that hashes each element with one algorithm.

arguments.name: algo
arguments.text: The hash algorithm. A unique prefix is accepted. md5 is the default.

arguments.name: errormode
arguments.text: stop raises DigestError. warn warns and returns NA. silent returns None.

translation.details: The returned function calls digest on each element and never returns raw bytes. A list of strings with serialize=False hashes each string. Pass integer values through integer() when the R input is an integer vector such as 1:5. A bytes object is one raw vector.
translation.value: A function that returns a list of hex strings.
translation.example:
from digest import getVDigest
sha1 = getVDigest(algo="sha1")
print(sha1(list("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz")))
